intended_use: The model is used for detecting fraudulent transactions based on an amount threshold, similar to an amount threshold classifier. The intended users are banks and online payment systems.
training_data: The model is trained using card_id and max_amount from [card_id, transaction count, avg_amount, max_amount, % card present, and event time]. It mainly looks at the maximum amount of transactions made by a card and does not consider the overall distribution of the transactions made by the card.
limitations: The model does not consider multiple transactions together when detecting fraud. A card could make multiple small transactions, each below the threshold, within a short period of time and bypass the amount threshold classifier. Because of this, the model cannot be fully trusted on its own for fraud detection.
ethical_considerations: A false positive, where a legitimate transaction is blocked, can make customers lose confidence in the banking system and may make them move to another service provider. In the case of a false negative, where a fraudulent transaction is not detected, the customer may lose money. Banks need to be responsible for how they classify and handle these cases.
